why: The note '+The following amendments stood in the name of ...' was credited to the member speaking, and the amendment lines after it with him. The note now has no speaker and ends the turn, so the lines after it have none. The lines under the asterisk-marked note before it keep his speaker; that is a known residue, not a ruling that he spoke them.

Title:SINGAPORE NATIONAL REFERENDUM BILL
MPs Speaking:Dr Goh Keng Swee (Minister for Finance); Dr Toh Chin Chye (Deputy Prime Minister and Leader of the House); Mr Chan Chee Seng (Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs); Mr K. M. Byrne (Minister for Health and Law); Mr Lee Kuan Yew (Prime Minister); Mr Ong Pang Boon (Minister for Home Affairs); Mr S. Ramaswamy (Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance); Dr Lee Siew Choh; Dr Sheng Nam Chin; Dr Thio Chan Bee; Madam Chan Choy Siong; Madam Hoe Puay Choo; Mr Chan Sun Wing; Mr David Marshall; Mr Low Por Tuck; Mr Ong Chang Sam; Mr Ong Eng Guan; Mr Tan Cheng Tong; Tun Lim Yew Hock; Mr John Mammen (Deputy Speaker); Sir George Oehlers (Mr Speaker);

SINGAPORE
NATIONAL REFERENDUM BILL


    Clause 32-

    Dr Lee Siew Choh: I move respectively the amendments* standing in my name. I see that the Member for Anson is also moving substantially the same amendments+, and I will leave the detailed arguments to him. For my part, we move the amendments for very simple reasons. We feel that the penalty is too severe. It is our contention that even if you want to penalise anybody, penalise him once but not twice. Sir, our fear is that immediately after a referendum, or not so very long after, a general election may be held. At any rate, the life of the Government does -


    * The following amendments stood in the name of Dr Lee Siew Choh:

    Amendment (i) :

    In page A13, line 36, after "years", to insert "or a fine".

    Amendment (ii) :

    In page A13, lines 37 and 38, to leave out "shall, by such conviction, become incapable, for a period of" and insert "may, on such conviction, be declared incapable for a period of up to".

    Amendment (iii) :

    In page A13, line 38, to leave out "of seven" and insert "not exceeding three".

    +The following amendments stood in the name of Mr David Marshall:

    Amendment (iv) :

    In page A13, to leave out lines 37 to 44 inclusive and insert "or a fine, and may by such conviction be declared incapable, for a period of up to seven years from the date of his conviction, of being registered as an elector or of voting at any referendum under this Ordinance or of voting at any election under the Singapore Legislative Assembly Elections Ordinance".

    Amendment (vi) :

    In page A14, line 6, to leave out from "year" to the end of line 14 and insert "or a fine".


    The Chairman: Order. The first amendment is,
